title: Designer Codes from GALA: Compact, Self-Dual, and Rate-1/2 QEC on Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
authors: Willers Yang, Casey Duckering, Arpit Dua
abstract: High rate quantum low-density parity-check codes on reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays can reduce the overhead of quantum error correction, but near-term devices support only hundreds of qubits with limited reconfigurability from a few crossed acousto-optic deflectors (AOD). A practical code must be compact in addition to low-overhead, with checks and logical gates mapping onto hardware-compatible physical instructions. We introduce the GALA codes, or Group-Action Lifts with Active orthogonality, that lifts over a product group $G = H_k \times C_m$ (or $H_k \ltimes C_m^k$). The small non-abelian factor $H_k$ supplies active orthogonality, reaching $1/2$ rate with above-weight distance, while the large abelian factor $C_m$ supplies symmetries that give code automorphisms and explicit, simple AOD move schedules. Hardware compatibility and logical capability thereby become customizable inputs to a code search rather than properties verified post-hoc, making GALA designer codes by construction. The GALA family contains several previously discovered rate-1/2 Kasai codes of Ref. [arXiv:2601.08824, arXiv:2604.16209] while exposing simpler parameter bounds, logical operations, and ZX-dual variants with AOD-compatible fold-transversal Clifford gates. Our search yields a compact self-dual $[[132, 30, 12]]$ with a small number of $4$-cycles (almost girth-6) and below $10^{-8}$ logical error rate (LER) for memory at $10^{-3}$ physical error rate, 3.1ms syndrome-extraction cycle and transversal Clifford gates; a girth-6, rate-$1/2$ $[[672, 336, 12]]$ with a 6.76ms cycle with below $10^{-10}$ LER (extrapolated) and rate-$1/2$ barrier-breaking $[[1752, 880, 14]]$ and $[[2232, 1120, 16]]$ with exactly certified distances greater than check weights and all smaller than previously known hardware compatible rate-1/2 codes.
summary: The paper introduces GALA codes, an algebraic framework for designing Quantum Error Correction codes tailored specifically for reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays. By constructing these codes using group lifts, the authors ensure that desirable properties like high rate and compatibility with physical gate operations are built in from the start. This yields several highly optimized code candidates suitable for near-term quantum computation.
main_problem: The core problem is designing Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes that are compact, self-dual, and maintain a high encoding rate ($\ge 1/2$) for implementation on near-term quantum hardware.
main_result: The authors introduce GALA codes, which provide an algebraically transparent construction method yielding several highly desirable instances, including a compact $[[132, 30, 12]]$ code with low logical error rates.
method: They use Group-Action Lifts over product groups ($G = H_k 	imes C_m$) to build codes. This construction makes hardware compatibility and desired logical operations customizable inputs rather than post-hoc checks.
model_or_system: The physical platform is reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays (RNAA) using qubits trapped in optical tweezers, with interactions controlled by acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). The code structure is defined algebraically via group theory lifts.
key_observables: Code parameters such as block length ($n$), logical qubit count ($k$), distance ($d$), encoding rate ($r$), and syndrome extraction cycle time (TQEC).
important_parameters: Rate $\ge 1/2$, girth $\ge 6$, low logical error rates ($	ext{LER} < 10^{-8}$), and compatibility with AOD-based physical gates.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to implement specific group structures ($H_k$ non-abelian, $C_m$ abelian) and relies on the algebraic framework of lifts over product groups.
figures_summary: Figures compare GALA codes against baselines regarding overhead and cycle time; one figure illustrates the syndrome extraction schedule using AOD sweeps; another details the logical gates ($	ext{H}_	au, 	ext{S}_	au$) for a specific code instance $[[132, 30, 12]]$ via its Gram matrix.
paper_structure: The paper introduces GALA codes by defining their algebraic construction using product groups. It then details the resulting properties, presents several optimized code instances in tables (e.g., TABLE S4), and finally analyzes the explicit implementation of logical gates on a representative code instance.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges abstract quantum error correction theory with concrete physical hardware constraints (AODs, limited qubits) by embedding hardware requirements into the code design process itself.

The code parameters in the legend are labeled as [n, k, d, w].

FIG. 2. GALA: a family of two-block codes lifted over a product group G = Hk ×Cm: the small non-abelian Hk supplies active orthogonality, achieving high rate and above-check-weight distance, while the large abelian Cm supplies symmetries that give both code automorphisms and parallel AOD row/column moves explicitly.

FIG. 3. Layout and syndrome-extraction schedule read off from the generators. Data atoms occupy a kp × Lq grid and check atoms a kp × Jq grid, writing Cm = Cp × Cq; the row coordinate carries the Hk index and the Cp component, the column coordinate carries the block index and the Cq compo- nent. Round i pairs each check with the data atom selected by the generator at that position of the block circulant, so the rearrangement between consecutive rounds is the transi- tion element FiF T i−1, which for a direct product factors into one rigid row translation σr,i and one rigid column translation σc,i (Eq. (4))—a single pair of AOD sweeps per round.

FIG. 4. GALA codes (lower-right is better). Left: compact codes with n ≤2500, rate ≥1/2, weight ≤12, girth ≥6. Best instances are highlighted in green, including the compact [[480, 240, 10]] and [[672, 336, 12]] and the above-weight [[1752, 880, 14]] and [[2232, 1120, 16]], all shorter than the co-designed Kasai baselines (black) [2]. Rate-1/2 pair-partition codes of Ref. [10] are shown for comparison. Right: ZX-dual codes with fold-transversal gates, notably a girth-4 [[132, 30, 12]] at rate 0.227 and a girth-6, rate-1/2 [[1056, 532, 12]].
